newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Investors bailed out of South African gold shares on Tuesday as the bullion price continued weak shaving nearly three percent off the index and taking it to its lowest closing level in 10 months.
But industrial shares were boosted by futures-related trade although dealers said were it not for this activity, the index would have ended flat on a lack of fresh factors.
"Golds are disappointing. Investors are reluctant to touch them," a dealer said.
He added that the crucial support for gold shares was at $372 per ounce which if broken the gold price could slide to $365 per ounce.
A firmer rand, which was last at 4.5850 bid on the dollar in after-hours trade was also seen negative for gold shares.
The gold index ended down 48.4 points, or 2.99 percent, at 1,572.9 -- its lowest closing level since January 19.
But the industrial board fared better.
"Industrials have been better. (But) if it wasn't for futures trade they would be dull...They are lacking proper direction," a dealer said.
Anglo results helped to lift sentiment in the afternoon following the release of half year results stronger than analysts' forecasts.
The stronger rand also helped gains in industrials, dealers said.
The industrial index added 60.3 points to 8,015.4 points and the all-share index was up 30 points to 6,721.3.

Trading on Tuesday was delayed by an hour at the open while the Johannesburg Stock Exchange tested its electronic trading system following two breakdowns on Monday. The market operated without hitches for the rest of the day.
Anglo added 125 cents to 257.25 rand, Absa rose 75 cents to 23.90 rand and De Beers gained 225 cents to 138 rand.
Dries dropped 250 cents 53.50 rand, Vaal Reefs shed 12.50 rand to 330 rand and Kloof lost 125 cents to 38 rand.
South African industrial index futures ended firm in quiet trade lifted by a strong Dow Jones, which surged past 6,500 level for first time on Monday night.
Golds were off their weakest morning levels but were still soft on bullion.
The December all-share contract was last at 6,145/80 from 6,048, the gold contract was at 1,110/17 from 1,146 and the industrial contract at 7,777/83 from 7,648.
